title: Epistemic States
purpose: Seed explicit epistemic states so Lantern distinguishes truth from what its evidence currently establishes, including unknown, conflict, possibility, support, challenge and suspension of judgment.

concepts.definition: The truth or falsity of a proposition in the relevant world/interpretation; Lantern's uncertainty about it is separate.
Lantern's current evidence-relative status for a proposition, distinct from the proposition's truth value.
Available evidence favors a proposition sufficiently for the applicable standard, without implying infallibility.
Available evidence counts against a proposition or a supporting argument.
Available information does not establish either the proposition or its negation.
Relevant evidence/claims support incompatible propositions within apparently overlapping scope and the conflict is not yet resolved.
A proposition is compatible with current constraints/evidence; possibility alone is not evidence that it is actual or likely.
A proposition is excluded by the applicable formal constraints or sufficiently established premises within scope.
A proposition follows in every permitted case under the declared formal/model assumptions.
A proposition has evidence/model support indicating higher likelihood under a declared probabilistic interpretation; not a synonym for true.
A deliberate decision not to accept or reject a proposition because evidence or standards are insufficient.
No relevant supporting evidence has been established; this is not automatically evidence for the negation.
Evidence expected under the proposition is missing or contrary evidence is present under conditions where that observation is informative.
A question remains open because required evidence, interpretation, scope or conflict resolution is incomplete.
A proposition/model has meaningful competing evidence or interpretations and remains under active dispute.
A calibrated degree of epistemic commitment or predictive probability under a specified interpretation; confidence is not truth.

guards.reason: Lack of resolution is not evidence that P is false.
Lack of resolution is not evidence that P is true.
Absence of evidence is not generally evidence of absence.
Compatibility with evidence does not establish likelihood.
High probability does not collapse uncertainty into truth.
Conflict contains information: incompatible evidence exists.
Source count alone ignores independence, quality, scope and provenance.
Epistemic confidence cannot grant permission or authority.
A confidence value is a model state, not a truth-maker.
Contrary evidence may lower support without conclusively refuting P.
Need for review does not itself reduce a claim to falsehood.

invariants: Truth status and epistemic status are separate dimensions.
UNKNOWN is neither TRUE nor FALSE.
CONFLICT is not ignorance; it records incompatible evidence/claims that require resolution.
POSSIBLE is weaker than PROBABLE and ACTUAL.
Confidence is not truth, authority, permission or source quality.
Absence of evidence becomes evidence of absence only when evidence was reasonably expected and the observation/test was capable of detecting it.
Source counts do not substitute for source independence, quality, provenance or scope.
Challenges update evidence status; they do not automatically erase or negate claims.
Scope differences must be checked before labeling claims contradictory.
Suspension of judgment is a valid outcome.
Staleness/review pressure is an epistemic-maintenance state, not a truth value.

provenance.authoring_basis: Core epistemology and uncertainty distinctions adapted to Lantern's provenance, contradiction, calibration and authority architecture.
